articles.title: Chrome Can Now Pull Booking Codes and Order Numbers From Your Gmail
articles.excerpt: Google's Gemini-powered enhanced autofill suggests flight bookings, tracking numbers and order details from your inbox as you fill forms — US-only, opt-in, and easy to switch off.
articles.nri_angle: Frequent US-India travellers are among the heaviest users of flight booking codes and tracking numbers the feature is built to surface.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: Use the three-dot menu, then Settings.
Select Enhanced autofill inside that section.

steps.step: Turn off 'Find and fill with Gemini'
steps.detail: This stops Gmail-based suggestions while leaving regular autofill intact.
In Gemini settings, under Connected Apps, disconnect Gmail to stop Gemini reading your mail at all.

data_cards.title: How to Turn Off Chrome's Gmail Autofill

articles.title: ISRO Launches NVS-03 Successfully, Restoring NavIC to Full Working Strength
articles.excerpt: GSLV-F18 placed the 2,232 kg navigation satellite in its intended orbit late on October 30, returning India's NavIC constellation to its four-satellite minimum and adding the smartphone-friendly L1 signal.
articles.image_caption: A second-generation NavIC satellite of the NVS series (file image). ISRO launched NVS-03, restoring NavIC to full working strength.
articles.nri_angle: NavIC's restored constellation and new L1 signal strengthen India's independent positioning system that diaspora travellers and devices increasingly rely on in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KLA Revenue Jumps 29 Percent as AI Demand Lifts Chip Equipment Market Toward 2027
articles.excerpt: KLA beat estimates with $4.14 billion in quarterly revenue and guided higher, as Gartner forecasts semiconductor sales approaching $1.94 trillion in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: AI chip demand is reshaping semiconductor jobs and investment flows that affect Indian technology workers and investors worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Opens 1.1 Million Sq Ft Block at Hyderabad Pocharam Campus
articles.excerpt: The new Pocharam block adds 10,000 seats and aims to support more than 13,000 additional employees under a hybrid model across a 450-acre campus.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian technology professionals abroad who collaborate with Hyderabad delivery teams, the expanded Pocharam campus adds capacity for global client work in AI, cloud and cybersecurity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Fires Up Ship 42 as Flight 15 Targets First-Ever Starship Tower Catch
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has completed static-fire tests on both stages of Starship Flight 15 — a full six-engine burn and a single-engine deorbit rehearsal on Ship 42, after a 33-engine firing of Booster 22 — ahead of a November launch that aims to catch both stages at the tower.
articles.image_caption: Starship's Ship 42 upper stage stands on its test stand at Starbase, Texas, in a graphic marking its six-engine static fire. Ship 42 completed full-duration six-engine and single-engine static fires ahead of Flight 15.
articles.nri_angle: Starship's progress toward full reusability is closely watched by India's growing space sector and diaspora engineers across the US aerospace industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ISRO's NVS-03 Launch Tonight Aims to Restore NavIC's Standalone Positioning
articles.excerpt: GSLV-F18 is set to lift off at 11:51 p.m. IST on October 30 carrying NVS-03, which would take NavIC to four working navigation satellites — the minimum for standalone positioning — after years of clock failures and the NVS-02 setback.
articles.image_caption: A GSLV rocket stands on the launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. GSLV-F18 is scheduled to carry the NVS-03 navigation satellite into orbit on the night of October 30.
articles.nri_angle: NavIC is the positioning system India's phones, vehicles and defence users rely on as a home-grown alternative to GPS; its recovery affects services across India and 1,500 km beyond its borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

ISRO review traces NVS-02 failure to a disconnected connector in a pyro-valve signal line
Government tells Parliament only 3 NavIC satellites provide navigation; 4 needed for standalone positioning

articles.title: Tech Stocks Slide Worldwide as Earnings Misses Revive Fears Over AI Spending
articles.excerpt: The Nasdaq fell 1.83% on Thursday and Asian chip stocks tumbled on Friday as Alphabet, Amazon and Intel misses turned a company earnings story into a global repricing of AI spending.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora investors holding US tech through index funds face index-level losses driven by the largest AI spenders, while the company-by-company split on cash flow now decides which tech holdings get repriced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eric Schmidt Says AI Could Let Large Companies Cut 20% of Staff
articles.excerpt: The former Google chief executive told the In Good Company podcast that a 10,000-person company may have 'a couple of thousand people who you don't need' once AI agents take over coordination work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Yulu Enters Nashik With 100 Electric Two-Wheelers for Delivery Riders
articles.excerpt: Nashik becomes Yulu's 13th city and its second in Maharashtra, as daily deliveries in the city double to about 25,000 and riders look for relief from petrol costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manohar Paluri Leaves Meta After 14 Years to Co-Found Warp Sciences
articles.excerpt: The IIIT Hyderabad graduate and former Meta AI vice president is now CTO of Warp Sciences, which raised $215 million to build AI-and-robotics chemistry labs for drug discovery in the US.
articles.nri_angle: Paluri's path from IIIT Hyderabad to Meta's AI leadership and now a US drug-discovery startup is a concrete example of Indian American technologists moving from platform AI into scientific infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Firms Hold Margins as AI Revenue Offsets Pricing Pressure
articles.excerpt: TCS kept its operating margin at 24%, HCLTech reached 18.2% EBIT and Infosys vowed to hold about 21%, even as AI revenue passed 10% of sales and clients demanded that AI savings be shared.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT firms employ millions in India and anchor many Indian-origin tech careers in the US; their shift from billable hours to AI-led delivery changes which skills command a premium on both sides.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startup Miraqules Wins SLINGSHOT 2026 Grand Prize in Singapore
articles.excerpt: The Indian medtech's StopBleed powder, designed to stop severe bleeding within about a minute, beat more than 5,000 startups to take the S$400,000 Startup SG Grant at SWITCH, according to CNA.
articles.nri_angle: A Bengaluru medtech winning Singapore's top deep-tech prize signals a route for Indian health-tech founders into Southeast Asian hospital and investor networks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Designed to stop bleeding within about a minute, according to the company.
Nanofibrous biomaterials made from clinically accepted biopolymers.
Designed for use in critical settings like battlefields and disaster zones.

articles.title: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 Puts 1,000 Startups in Front of Global Investors
articles.excerpt: The November 17-19 summit expects 60,000 visitors and 700 speakers, with a Startup Pavilion, Investor Connect matchmaking and a new AI and robotics pavilion.
articles.nri_angle: The summit's Investor Connect and India-USA Tech Conclave are a direct route for diaspora founders and investors into India's startup ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 opens at BIEC
Summit day two; Investor Connect and startup stages continue
Final day; Future Makers Conclave and unicorn felicitation

articles.title: Freshworks Buys Robusta to Add AI Outage Investigation to Freshservice
articles.excerpt: The undisclosed deal brings Robusta Dev's AI root-cause analysis into Freshservice, alongside FireHydrant, with engineers approving any production change.
articles.nri_angle: Freshworks, founded in Chennai and run for a global customer base, is a flagship Indian-origin SaaS company; its AI operations push affects IT teams worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CERT-In Warns of High-Risk Flaws in iPhone, Mac and Other Apple Products
articles.excerpt: India's cybersecurity agency says vulnerabilities across iOS, macOS, Safari, watchOS, tvOS and visionOS could allow code execution and data theft — users should update now.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora Apple users are directly in CERT-In's target audience and should install Apple's latest updates on every device.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: CERT-In issues advisory on Apple vulnerabilities.
CERT-In issued a similar high-severity advisory.
CERT-In issued another warning regarding Apple products.

articles.title: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, Its Strongest Model for Coding and Cyber Defense
articles.excerpt: Carbon tops the Artificial Analysis index at 59 and leads key cybersecurity benchmarks, but access starts with a vetted group of cyber defenders, not the public.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora engineering teams gain a stronger coding and security model to plan around, though public access is not yet open.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nalwa Aero Flight-Tests Box-Wing Electric Aircraft in Punjab Milestone
articles.excerpt: The Punjab startup's scaled eVTOL demonstrated hovering and forward flight with an all-tilting-rotor system, as it works towards a five-seat aircraft for passengers, air ambulances and cargo.
articles.nri_angle: The programme was built by returnee talent — founder Kuljeet Singh Sandhu left Canada for India and CTO Nelson Salas relocated from the United States — a reverse-migration pattern familiar to diaspora engineers weighing a move back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Warren Demands Anthropic Answers on Existential AI Risks Before IPO
articles.excerpt: Senator Elizabeth Warren has given Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei until November 3 to answer four pages of questions on the catastrophic risks, partnerships and near-$2 trillion valuation disclosed in the company's S-1 filing.
articles.image_caption: Senator Elizabeth Warren, ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-origin AI engineers and US-based Indian investors with retirement accounts, Warren's challenge tests how a frontier lab's own safety warnings will be priced — and automatically bought by index funds — once Anthropic lists.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Advanced AI could pose catastrophic risks to humanity.
AI models may assist in developing bioweapons.
How will Anthropic prevent existential threats?
Details on partnerships with Amazon and Broadcom.
Justification for a valuation approaching $2 trillion.

articles.title: India Plans New Framework To Bring Startups Into Government Procurement
articles.excerpt: Speaking at the National Startup Awards 6.0 curtain-raiser, DPIIT officials said procurement relaxations for startups already exist but are under-used, and that a new framework is being prepared with three other ministries.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora founders considering building or supplying from India, the promised framework would widen a procurement route that DPIIT-recognised startups can already enter through GeM.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar's GomatiRoots Turns Homemade Badi Into Brand, Wins Shuru Kar Funding
articles.excerpt: Shital Kumari's Patna startup, built around Bihar's traditional lentil badi, has received Rs 1 lakh through YourStory's Shuru Kar initiative after recording Rs 32 lakh in revenue in its first financial year.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers who buy regional Indian foods online, GomatiRoots' stated long-term ambition to export Bihari badi is the part of its plan to watch.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ex-Meta AI Director Rohit Patel Launches Ndoc to Take On Office and Google Workspace
articles.excerpt: After eight years at Meta, most recently as a director at Meta Superintelligence Labs, Patel is building an AI-native workspace that unifies documents, data and presentations — and plans to open-source its file format so users are never locked in.
articles.image_caption: Rohit Patel speaks on stage at a technology conference. Patel left Meta after eight years to launch Ndoc, an AI-native alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American AI leader leaving a Big Tech lab to challenge Microsoft and Google is the diaspora's founder pipeline in action.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SK Hynix Profit Jumps Sevenfold to Record on AI Memory Demand
articles.excerpt: Operating profit hit 83.3 trillion won in the third quarter as HBM4 shipments and server memory demand pushed revenue past 100 trillion won for the first time, and the Nvidia supplier unveiled a 100 trillion won shareholder return plan.
articles.nri_angle: AI memory demand is reshaping chip earnings that Indian tech investors and semiconductor professionals track closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Says AI Alignment Will Not Simply Fall Out of Scaling
articles.excerpt: On the 20VC podcast, Microsoft's CEO said capabilities have scaled as he expected but alignment has not, and urged companies to treat models as insider threats wrapped in deterministic controls.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in a portrait from the Harvard Business School AI Institute. Nadella told the 20VC podcast he no longer believes AI alignment will emerge automatically as models scale.
articles.nri_angle: Nadella, Microsoft's Indian-American CEO, is a closely watched voice for Indian and diaspora technologists, and his call to engineer alignment shifts work toward evaluations, controls and oversight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Disruptive Closes $10 Billion Flagship Fund for Ten Late-Stage Bets
articles.excerpt: The Dallas firm founded by Alex Davis is abandoning deal-by-deal vehicles for its first pooled fund, planning checks of up to $1 billion each in AI, defense and software companies.
articles.nri_angle: The fund's focus on AI and defense concentrates new late-stage capital in sectors where Indian founders and engineers are heavily represented, though the sources name no India-specific investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Leaders Hold Key Roles as Anthropic Heads for Its IPO
articles.excerpt: From CFO Krishna Rao, who signed the IPO filing, to Bengaluru-born CTO Rahul Patil and Claude Code co-creator Sid Bidasaria, Indian-origin executives sit at the centre of Anthropic's finances, technology and governance as it prepares to list.
articles.nri_angle: Anthropic's finance, technology and trust leadership includes several Indian-origin executives, and its IPO filing flags US immigration policy as a risk to hiring the Indian engineers the AI industry relies on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Goes Live With Syngenta SAP Core for 10,000 Staff in 80 Countries
articles.excerpt: Crop Protection Core replaces multiple ERP systems with one SAP S/4HANA platform covering research, manufacturing, supply chain, regulatory, finance and commercial operations.
articles.image_caption: Infosys headquarters in Bengaluru. Infosys has gone live with Syngenta's SAP core for 10,000 staff
articles.nri_angle: The delivery strengthens Bengaluru-based Infosys's standing in large global transformations, a business that employs and trains Indian engineers at scale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA Artemis III Will Launch Three Rockets to Test Two Lunar Landers
articles.excerpt: The 14-day Earth-orbit mission in summer 2027 will dock Orion with Blue Origin's Blue Moon and SpaceX's Starship, clearing the way for a 2028 lunar landing.
articles.nri_angle: Artemis sets the timetable for lunar science and commercial work that Indian researchers, engineers and space firms are positioning to join.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: NASA outlines flight plan for Artemis III
Artemis IV attempts crewed lunar landing

articles.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Rogue Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens With No Permissions
articles.excerpt: Enclave researchers found an app with zero permissions could impersonate Teams and have Authenticator hand over work-account tokens; Microsoft patched the flaw as CVE-2026-80097, CVSS 8.6, in version 6.2606.4246.
articles.nri_angle: Anyone using Authenticator for a work Microsoft 365 account on Android should update to 6.2606.4246 or later now.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: Check you are on version 6.2606.4246 or later in the Google Play Store.
The attack needed a malicious app installed on the same device; delete apps you do not recognise.

steps.step: Ask your IT team to enforce the minimum version
steps.detail: Help Net Security notes MDM can enforce 6.2606.4246 as the floor for company devices.

data_cards.title: How to Protect Your Work Account

articles.title: Apple Promotes Indian-Origin Rajesh Ambati and Two Others to Engineering Vice President
articles.excerpt: Rajesh Ambati, Louie Sanguinetti and Derek Shaeffer became vice presidents for connectivity in Apple's October promotions, as display veterans Wei Chen and John Zhong step back to adviser roles under CEO John Ternus.
articles.nri_angle: Ambati's promotion is another senior engineering elevation for an Indian-origin leader at a US technology giant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Named a Leader in Everest Group's Agentic Process Automation Assessment
articles.excerpt: Everest Group's 2026 APA PEAK Matrix assessed 26 providers and placed TCS among seven Leaders, citing its WisdomNext, ignio and Cognitive Automation platforms.
articles.nri_angle: For the large Indian-origin workforce in global IT services, TCS's agentic-AI push signals how the industry's work is shifting from labour-based delivery to AI-agent platforms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wall Street Lines Up $63 Billion to Finance Broadcom Chips for Anthropic
articles.excerpt: Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley will fund a special purpose vehicle that buys Broadcom XPU accelerators and networking gear and leases them to Anthropic, with deliveries starting in 2027 and Broadcom guaranteeing the senior debt.

sources.label: The Wall Street Journal via Morningstar (Dow Jones Newswires)

articles.nri_angle: The scale of Wall Street financing for AI compute underlines how much capital is flowing into the US AI infrastructure that employs large numbers of Indian-origin engineers and researchers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts to 60,000 Employees Across Four Countries
articles.excerpt: The Voluntary Exit Offer covers about a quarter of Microsoft's 223,000-person workforce in the U.S., Canada, India and the U.K., with decisions due in the first week of December.
articles.nri_angle: The buyout offer covers Microsoft staff in India as well as Indian employees in the U.S., Canada and the U.K., at level 70 and below on participating teams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'There Won't Be Real Jobs Left': Engineer Considers Farming Amid AI Fears
articles.excerpt: A veteran software engineer's viral post about quitting for farming captures tech's AI anxiety — but WEF and Stanford data show a redistribution hitting young developers hardest, not a disappearance of work.
articles.image_caption: Andrew Ng at WSJ CIO Dinner on AI. AI pioneer Andrew Ng offered the counter-case at the NDTV World Summit on October 22: US software engineer postings are up because AI makes engineers more productive, and reskilling, not exit, is the answer.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Steve Jurvetson via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
articles.nri_angle: For Indian IT professionals in India and the US diaspora, the data points to reskilling toward AI deployment, security and architecture rather than exiting the profession.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: 40% of job skills will change by 2030

articles.title: NASA's Swift Telescope Ends 22-Year Mission, Heads For Atmospheric Re-Entry
articles.excerpt: The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory made its final observation on October 20 after atmospheric drag pulled it to 171 miles, ending a two-year mission that lasted more than 10 times as long.
articles.nri_angle: Swift's open 12-terabyte archive will keep supporting researchers worldwide, including Indian-origin astronomers in US and European astrophysics groups, for decades.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Madras Scientist Helps Show a Spinning Molecule Can Boost Current 100-Fold
articles.excerpt: A helicene molecule trapped between gold electrodes rotates when voltage is applied — and its rotation opens high-conductance shapes that raise current up to 100 times, in a Nature study co-authored by IIT Madras's Anil Kumar Singh.
articles.nri_angle: The study puts an IIT Madras physicist in a five-country Nature paper on molecular machines, a field Indian researchers and students abroad work in directly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canva Launches Craft, Its First In-House Image Model Built for Design
articles.excerpt: Trained on millions of human-made templates instead of photographs, Craft plans a layout before it renders — and is live now in Dream Lab and the Canva API.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Ravens freak0624 via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: Canva is a daily production tool for Indian and diaspora creators and small businesses; a design-trained model with legible text directly affects their social, menu and presentation work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft and Opella Build Lumen to Verify AI Health Content at Scale
articles.excerpt: The agentic platform uses 14 specialized agents to check product claims, medical facts and legal mentions across Opella's 21,000 AI-generated assets, with human experts keeping final approval.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft headquarters in Redmond, Washington (file photo). Microsoft is building Lumen with Opella to verify AI-generated health content at scale.
articles.nri_angle: The platform is a reference case for Indian and diaspora health-tech and pharma marketing teams facing the same problem: AI content volume rising faster than medical and legal review capacity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startup Funding Dips Below $100 Million as Deeptech Eyes Global Markets
articles.excerpt: YourStory counted $96 million across 15 deals in a soft October week, while TechSparks panellists told deeptech founders that India alone is too small a market.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora founders and investors in Indian tech, the soft funding week and the deeptech panel's message point the same way: the next generation of Indian startups must sell and raise globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startup Funding Falls 22% in a Week as AI Takes Half the Money
articles.excerpt: Startups raised about $184 million (₹1,747 crore) across 17 deals between October 19 and 23, with two cheques — Even Healthcare and Different — accounting for more than half the total.
articles.nri_angle: Funding concentration in AI and healthtech shapes where Indian tech jobs and founder opportunities are growing, a pipeline many diaspora founders and investors track closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: iPhone Duo Screens Crack Along the Hinge Within Hours of $1,999 Foldable's Launch
articles.excerpt: A handful of early owners report inner displays splitting at the fold — one after fewer than 20 openings. Apple has not commented, and the cause is unknown.
articles.nri_angle: At $1,999, the Duo is a major purchase for tech buyers in the diaspora; knowing the warranty and return position matters more than the launch hype.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: Keep the device in its current position to avoid widening the crack.
Photograph the inner display and note when it happened and how many times the phone had been opened.
Hinge failure from normal use is covered by the one-year warranty; launch-week buyers are also inside the 14-day return window.

data_cards.title: If Your iPhone Duo Screen Cracks at the Hinge

articles.title: Bitcoin Hovers Near $80,000 as ETF Outflows and $100 Oil Weigh on Crypto
articles.excerpt: Ethereum held near $2,370 as $636 million left US spot Bitcoin ETFs, $467 million in leveraged bets were liquidated, and crude above $100 kept pressure on risk assets.
articles.image_caption: A Bitcoin ATM outlet in Wroclaw, Poland. Bitcoin hovered near $80,000 as ETF outflows and $100 oil weighed on crypto markets.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora investors holding crypto directly or through US spot Bitcoin ETFs face the same ETF-flow and rates pressures driving the sell-off.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Listing 'AI-Proof' Jobs and Sectors It Wants to Lead Globally, Goyal Says
articles.excerpt: Speaking in Berlin, Piyush Goyal said the Commerce Ministry is identifying professions AI cannot replace — handicrafts and handloom among them — and sectors where India can take a global lead.
articles.nri_angle: The ministry's AI-proof list signals which India-facing skills and services sectors will get policy backing, relevant to diaspora professionals in AI-exposed roles and wellness and finance entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Handicrafts: No AI can replace this sector.
Handloom: Essential for preserving traditional skills.
Culinary Arts: Human creativity is irreplaceable.
Tourism: Personal touch is vital in this industry.
